name: Canoes, Convicts and Kingdoms: A History of the Pacific
description: The navigators who settled a third of the globe by canoe, the Europeans who followed them, the colonies they made, and the nations of Australia, New Zealand and the islands.

checkpoints.name: The first voyagers
checkpoints.note: Aboriginal peoples have lived on the Australian continent for tens of thousands of years, and Uluru is sacred ground. Around 1000 BCE sailors in Polynesian voyaging canoes reach Tonga and Samoa, steering by stars and swells, and over centuries they push east to the Hawaiian Islands. The Tu'i Tonga rise.

checkpoints.name: Stone cities and statues
checkpoints.note: On Pohnpei rulers build Nan Madol on reefs, and on Easter Island the Rapa Nui carve the moai. The Maori settle New Zealand, where the haka takes shape and the giant moa is hunted to extinction. The Tu'i Tonga hold sway over islands far around Tonga.

checkpoints.name: Strangers from Europe
checkpoints.note: The Magellan-Elcano circumnavigation crosses the Pacific in 1520 and 1521. Abel Tasman sights Tasmania and New Zealand in 1642. On his first voyage James Cook charts New Zealand and Australia's east coast, and he is killed in Hawaii in 1779. In 1787 the First Fleet sails for New South Wales.

checkpoints.name: Colonies and kingdoms
checkpoints.note: Sydney is founded as a convict colony in 1788, and the Bounty mutiny follows in 1789. Kamehameha I unites the Kingdom of Hawaii. Missionaries write down the Maori language, and the Treaty of Waitangi is signed in 1840. Gold rushes bring the Eureka Rebellion, and the All Blacks first tour in 1884.

checkpoints.name: New nations at war
checkpoints.note: The federation of Australia creates a nation in 1901, New Zealand becomes a dominion in 1907, and Canberra is founded as a capital in 1913. Australian and New Zealand troops fight at Gallipoli in 1915. Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941 brings war to the Pacific, and Midway turns it in 1942.

checkpoints.name: The island nations
checkpoints.note: Hawaii becomes an American state in 1959. Samoa wins its independence in 1962, the first Pacific island country to do so, followed by Fiji and Tonga in 1970 and Papua New Guinea in 1975. Sydney Opera House opens in 1973 as a symbol of a new Australia.
